member.name: T:NAudio.Midi.IMidiInstrument
member.summary: An instrument that consumes MIDI events and renders audio: MIDI in via , audio out via the pull model. Implemented by the NAudio.Sampler engine, and the seam for any other MIDI-driven renderer (a synthesiser, a hosted VST instrument, …) to plug into the same playback hosts: (timeline playback), (faster-than-real-time render) and (live input from another thread).
member.remarks: Unless an implementation documents otherwise, it is single-threaded: and Read must be called from the same thread, and events take effect on the audio rendered by subsequent Read calls. Hosts that interleave events and audio within a block (as does) get sample-accurate timing by rendering in segments between events.

member.name: T:NAudio.Midi.LiveMidiInstrument
member.summary: Plays an from a live MIDI source (a hardware keyboard, an on-screen keyboard, etc.). Unlike , which reads events from a timeline on the audio thread, events here arrive asynchronously from other threads (a MIDI input callback, the UI thread, …).
member.remarks:
Incoming events are placed on a lock-free queue by and drained on the audio thread at the start of each , so the (single-threaded) wrapped instrument is only ever touched from one thread. Events therefore take effect at the next block boundary; the resulting latency is just the output buffer size, which is the expected behaviour for a live, pull-driven instrument.
The wrapper is itself an whose is the thread-safe, deferred , so hosts can treat live-bridged and directly-driven instruments uniformly.

member.name: T:NAudio.Midi.SequencedMidiPlayer
member.summary: Plays an of MIDI events on an , driven by a . Unlike (which spawns a sample provider per event into a mixer), this drives a single stateful polyphonic instrument: on each it dispatches the buffer's MIDI events to the instrument at their exact frame offset, rendering the instrument in segments between events so timing is sample-accurate within the block.
member.remarks: The steady-state path performs no heap allocations and takes no lock on the timeline: event queries run over 's lock-free immutable snapshot, and the per-buffer event list and dispatch delegate are allocated once up front.
